description.narrative:
The Nakuru Potato Cooperative Union Limited (NPCU) is a union of 13 primary cooperatives headquartered in Muchorwi, Turi Ward, Molo Sub-County, Nakuru, Kenya. Governed by a seven-member Board of Management, the Union also has Executive, Supervisory, and Marketing Committees, and employs eight staff members. NPCU represents 4,363 registered farmers across five sub-counties: Njoro, Molo, Kuresoi South, Kuresoi North, and Gilgil. Operating under its by-laws, the Union is guided by a range of policy documents covering strategic planning, gender, environment, finance, procurement, human resources, elections, and ethical conduct. Its core activities include ware potato production, seed potato multiplication, and collective marketing. NPCU supports farmers by linking them to credit providers, input suppliers, training institutions, and markets, while also introducing new contract-based potato varieties for the processing sector.
Historically dependent on commissions from sales, the Union has faced revenue challenges due to market inefficiencies and reduced production caused by high input costs. To strengthen sustainability, NPCU is expanding into certified seed production as a regulated seed merchant under KEPHIS. It is currently bulking certified seed and managing a fleet of potato production machinery to generate income. Additional partnerships, such as with Hifadhi Africa for subsidized soil testing, enhance service delivery. NPCU has also contributed to key regulatory frameworks, including the Crops (Irish Potato) Regulations of 2019 and the Nakuru County Potato Sub-Sector Strategy
